propositions: Four test guards (test_the_provenance_analysis_can_see_the_sites_it_judges, test_no_run_request_inherits_the_raw_config_model, test_every_unfollowable_site_is_registered_with_a_reason, test_neither_registry_has_stale_entries) each independently call _run_request_sites(), repeating the same whole-tree AST analysis four times per test session

Within each call to _run_request_sites(), the _verdict() function re-walks the entire src/rebar tree and re-parses every file once per parameter-provenance site being analyzed, causing ~8,033 redundant parses in a single scan
_functions() also parses the entire src/rebar tree, contributing a second layer of internal repetition within each _run_request_sites() call
The AST analysis is a pure function of committed src/rebar source code with no test mutations or dependencies on patches consulted by the scan, making caching safe

Caching _run_request_sites() as a session-scoped fixture and memoizing per-file parses via _parsed() reduces wall-clock time from 50.14s to 5.96s (-88%) and single-scan time from 11.83s to 4.14s (-65%)
